claims.text: Pre-aging HfNbTaTiZr at 700 °C induces local chemical ordering.
Local chemical ordering alters local lattice parameters.
Local chemical ordering alters local thermal expansion coefficients.
Spatial variations in lattice parameters and thermal expansion produce microscale thermal expansion mismatch.
Thermal expansion mismatch between ordered regions and the surrounding matrix generates internal thermal stresses at elevated temperature.
The resulting internal thermal stresses modify dislocation mobility.
The resulting internal thermal stresses modify the alloy's elastic response.
The proposed ordering–thermal-mismatch mechanism controls both creep behavior and thermoelastic anomalies.
The solution-treated initial state is fully disordered and has uniform lattice parameters and thermal expansion behavior.
The 700 °C pre-aging temperature lies within a previously studied 600–800 °C aging window.
Relative to the solution-treated baseline, pre-aged specimens will have lower creep rates.
Relative to the solution-treated baseline, pre-aged specimens will have increased stiffness, especially at lower temperatures.
Pre-aged specimens will exhibit a more pronounced temperature dependence of elastic moduli than solution-treated specimens.
Thermal expansion measurements will show greater spatial heterogeneity corresponding to the degree of chemical ordering.
Ordering is activated near 600 °C, and its proposed mechanical effects extend through the 1250 °C creep regime.
The mechanism is applicable only when local ordering predominates over effects such as second-phase precipitation.
Residual stresses and precipitate formation may also contribute to thermal expansion mismatch and mechanical behavior.
